newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady to firm, August bid.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - T-bond vols steady to firm, August bid.

text.p: Implied volatilities for U.S. Treasury bond options were steady to firmer in late trade, with bids centering on the gamma-rich shorter maturities, dealers said.
A corrective downturn in bond prices and caution ahead of the July 1-2 Federal Open Market Committee meeting buoyed demand for the shorter dates, particularly the downside strikes, they added.
Implied volatility for August T-bond futures options, which expire in about three weeks, blipped up about 0.2 point to around 8.0 percent.
"Generally, they're looking pretty steady but up a little in August," said a brokerage firm trader at the Chicago Board of Trade.
He noted that a pickup in demand for gamma, which provides bigger delta swings for volatility traders and quicker premium acceleration, was not unexpected before an FOMC meeting.
Still, a widely held expectation that the Federal Reserve will not raise interest rates at next week's meeting kept volatilities from surging across the board.
September volatility was steady at around 8.3 percent and even in August options, low-delta calls saw a lot of selling.

Traders said the selling probably reflected perception that September futures would be consolidative and unlikely to test last Friday's 112-24/32 high near term but not violent enough to make low-delta puts too attractive.
An investment bank was said to have sold 5,000 contracts of August 112 calls.

"You've got to get another wave of selling and retest 110-1/2 or so to really put fear into people's minds," a bank affiliate trader said. He was referring to a trendline support for September futures, which ended down 18/32 at 111-5/32.
At the shorter end of the yield curve, Eurodollar volatilities were generally steady to softer mainly because Eurodollar futures were more resilient than bonds.
Implied volatility for September Eurodollar futures options was off 0.2 point at 9.4 percent, while March was steady at 11.5 percent.

Back month futures were seen pressured by swap-related selling stemming from corporate bond issuance and huge 10-year note selling that was said to have triggered Wednesday's late slide in the bond market.
